title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
This sheet is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is page '-5-' of an English typescript, photographed upside down. By its content and numbering it is almost certainly a preliminary draft of R. Hartshorne's 'Residues and Duality' (the notes from Grothendieck's duality theory), Chapter II, section on Hom and Ext. Grothendieck evidently reused the sheet's other side for his handwritten notes on the Lefschetz-type standard conjectures (neighbouring pages on C(X), A^0(X×Y), Λ, hyperplane sections).

Content, step by step:
(1) End of a proof of a statement. On a locally noetherian prescheme X, if L is coherent and M is coherent (resp. quasi-coherent), then Ext^i(L,M) is coherent (resp. quasi-coherent) for all i.
- The question is local, so choose a presentation 0→L'→O^p→L→0 with L' coherent.
- The long exact Ext sequence, together with Ext^i(O^p,M)=0 for i≥1, gives Hom(O^p,M)→Hom(L',M)→Ext^1(L,M)→0. Hence Ext^1(L,M) is coherent (resp. quasi-coherent), using the case i=0 applied to L'.
- It also gives Ext^i(L,M)≅Ext^{i-1}(L',M) for i>1. Dimension shifting and induction on i then finish the proof.
(2) Corollary 2.2. Let L· ∈ D(X) have coherent cohomology and M· ∈ D^+(X) have coherent (resp. quasi-coherent) cohomology. Assume either (a) L· ∈ D^-, or (b) L· ∈ D^+ and Ext^i(F,M·)=0 for all coherent F and all i>n_0 (a finite injective-dimension-type condition). Then RHom·(L·,M·) has coherent (resp. quasi-coherent) cohomology.
- The proof is left as an exercise via the 'lemma on way-out functors'.
- In case (b) the condition makes the functor way-out in both directions.

This matches Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, II.3 (cf. Prop. II.3.3 and the way-out functor lemma I.7.1). It serves the foundational set-up of coherent duality.
errors: No mathematical errors. The dimension-shifting argument is correct (it uses Ext^i(O^p,M)=0 for i≥1).
The corollary is correct as stated and agrees with the published version in Residues and Duality.

ideas.what: Coherence of local Ext sheaves Ext^i(L,M) for L,M coherent on a locally noetherian scheme, by local presentation and dimension shifting
ideas.where_published: EGA 0_III (12.3.3 area); also Hartshorne, Residues and Duality II.3

ideas.what: RHom(L·,M·) has coherent/quasi-coherent cohomology under boundedness hypotheses (L bounded above, or L bounded below and M of finite injective dimension on coherent sheaves)
ideas.modern_name: RHom: D_c^-(X)^op × D^+_{qc}(X) → D^+_{qc}(X); way-out functor lemma
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, written up by Hartshorne (Residues and Duality, 1966)
ideas.where_published: Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, LNM 20, Ch. II §3 (Prop. 3.3) and Ch. I §7 (way-out functors)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a stray (reused) sheet of Hartshorne's Residues and Duality typescript containing standard, published foundational material. It has no connection to the standard-conjecture notes on the surrounding pages beyond being scrap paper. The only minor historical interest is that it documents Grothendieck reusing a draft of Hartshorne's notes, c. 1966.
transcription_corrections: The page image is rotated 180°; the transcription correctly reads it upright.
The handwritten '40' sits in the bottom-left margin of the image (archive page number); it is not part of the text.
The text is an English typescript (Hartshorne's Residues and Duality draft), not Grothendieck's French manuscript; the transcription is otherwise accurate.
